label: Contingent truths have sufficient reasons
summary: The pinned Latta translation gives the general principle in §32, distinguishes contingent truths in §33, and applies sufficient reason to contingent truths in §36. §§37–38 separately argue for a final reason beyond the contingent series. The local target only asks for a reason token.
blocker: The principle addresses the recorded brute-contingency alternative by requiring a reason for the truth in question, even when unknown. Applying it requires a world-indexed contingent existent to yield a fact of the kind Leibniz covers and its sufficient reason to supply a token for the same existence fact in the model’s explains relation. The model does not require that a token be sufficient in Leibniz’s sense.
